The Embedding Class in LangChain
Using the Embedding Class in LangChain for Text Vector Representations and Its Common Interface for Interacting with Various Embedding Providers
In natural language processing (NLP), an “embedding” (we can translate as: text embedding) is a dense representation of words, phrases, or documents in a low-dimensional vector space. These embeddings are useful for many tasks, including semantic search, where we look for texts that are similar in the vector space.
In other words, ‘embeddings’ create a vector representation of a piece of text. This is useful because it means we can think about text in vector space and do things like semantic search, where we look for pieces of text that are most similar in the vector space.
Explaining “embedding” to a Child
Imagine you and your friends invented a secret language where every word you normally use is replaced by a different symbol or image. So, the word “dog” might be represented by a drawing of a bone, the word “book” might be a drawing of a tree (because books are made of paper and paper comes from trees), and so on.
Now, what “embedding” does in the field of natural language processing (NLP) is very similar to that. It takes words or phrases and transforms them into something the computer can understand better: a list of numbers, which we call a vector. For the computer, these numbers represent the word or phrase very well, just like the bone can represent “dog” in your secret language.
The reason we do this is that when words or phrases are converted into vectors, the computer can measure how similar or different they are, just like you could say two drawings are similar or different. This is useful for many things, like helping the computer understand what you’re saying or writing, or helping it find relevant information on the internet.
The Embedding Class
The Embedding class in LangChain is a class designed to interface with embeddings, meaning it provides a common interface for interacting with various embedding providers, such as OpenAI, Cohere, Hugging Face, etc.
This class exposes two methods: embed_documents and embed_query.
•
embed_documents is used when you have multiple documents and want to get the vector representation for all of them. For example, you can use this method to prepare a set of documents for semantic search by pre-computing the embeddings for all of them.
•
embed_query is used to get the vector representation of a single document or query. This representation can then be used to find similar documents in a set of pre-embedded documents.
The main difference is that these two methods have different interfaces: one works with multiple documents, while the other works with a single document.
Integrations
There are several integrations available for text embeddings in LangChain, each corresponding to a different embedding provider, such as Aleph Alpha, AzureOpenAI, Cohere, Hugging Face Hub, and others. This means you can use the same code to work with different embedding providers, just by changing the provider you use.
The following integrations exist for text embedding:
•
Aleph Alpha
•
AzureOpenAI
•
Cohere
•
Fake Embeddings
•
Hugging Face Hub
•
InstructEmbeddings
•
Jina
•
Llama-cpp
•
OpenAI
•
SageMaker Endpoint Embeddings
•
Self Hosted Embeddings
•
Sentence Transformers Embeddings
•
TensorflowHub
